commonsFile: File:Qasr al-Farid, Hegra (Madain Salih), 1st cent. CE, Saudi Arabia (24).jpg
attribution: Richard Mortel — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Qasr al-Farid, a lone Nabataean tomb carved into a freestanding sandstone outcrop in the desert at Hegra
caption: Qasr al-Farid, the unfinished 'Lonely Castle' tomb at Hegra (Madain Salih), the centrepiece of the AlUla concept. Its isolation in an empty sandstone plain explains why Hegra is the headline site of this route, which is currently shown for information only.

attribution: Saudi Press Agency (SPA) — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Jabal AlFil (Elephant Rock), a sandstone formation shaped like an elephant, rising from the desert floor near AlUla
caption: Jabal AlFil near AlUla, a natural sandstone landmark. It shows the eroded rock scenery around the AlUla base, which is the other draw of the area besides the tombs.

attribution: Z thomas — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Ancient inscriptions carved on the sandstone canyon walls at Jabal Ikmah, AlUla
caption: Jabal Ikmah, an open-air 'library' of Dadanite and Lihyanite inscriptions on the walls of a canyon near AlUla. It is the main epigraphic stop of the concept and the reason for the scholarly side of the route.

commonsFile: File:Ibex, Jubbah rock art site, Saudi Arabia.jpg
attribution: Richard Mortel — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Ancient ibex petroglyph carved into a rock face at the Jubbah rock art site near Hail
caption: An ibex carved into the rock at Jubbah, in the Hail region, part of the UNESCO-listed rock art landscape. It represents the Neolithic and later carvings that pull the route towards northern Saudi Arabia.

attribution: Richard Mortel — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Ancient camel petroglyph at the Jubbah rock art site near Hail
caption: A camel petroglyph at Jubbah. Together with the ibex and the human figures, the carvings record thousands of years of life by an ancient lake basin at the edge of the Nafud desert.

attribution: Radosław Botev — CC BY 3.0 pl, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Mud-brick Najdi architecture and earthen walls in the At-Turaif district of Diriyah near Riyadh
caption: At-Turaif in Diriyah, the first Saudi capital and a UNESCO World Heritage mud-brick quarter on the edge of Riyadh. It is the cultural stop at the start or end of the concept, close to the airport.

commonsFile: File:Qasr al-Farid, Hegra (Madain Salih), 1st cent. CE, Saudi Arabia (12).jpg
attribution: Richard Mortel — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Facade of the Nabataean tomb Qasr al-Farid at Hegra, seen from close range
caption: A closer view of the Qasr al-Farid facade at Hegra. The carved cornice and doorway, cut from a single outcrop, give a sense of the scale of the monument.

attribution: Radosław Botev — CC BY 3.0 pl, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Restored earthen walls and towers of At-Turaif in Diriyah
caption: Restored walls and towers of At-Turaif, Diriyah, which show the Najdi mud-brick style used by the first Saudi state. The district is the best-preserved example of the Najd plateau's historic architecture in this concept.

commonsFile: File:Jabal al-Ahmar Necropolis, Hegra (Mada'in Salih), the kingdom's second Nabatean capital after Petra, Saudi Arabia.jpg
attribution: Following Hadrian — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Rock-cut Nabataean tombs of the Jabal al-Ahmar necropolis at Hegra, set against a sandstone hill
caption: The Jabal al-Ahmar necropolis at Hegra, where 18 tombs cut into red sandstone include recent discoveries. Together with Qasr al-Bint it shows that Hegra is more than a single monument.

commonsFile: File:Qasr al-Bint necropolis, Hegra (Mada'in Salih), the kingdom's second Nabatean capital after Petra, Saudi Arabia.jpg
attribution: Carole Raddato from FRANKFURT, Germany — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Monumental Nabataean tomb facades of the Qasr al-Bint necropolis at Hegra
caption: The Qasr al-Bint necropolis at Hegra, the most monumental group of tombs on the site, with facades up to 16 metres high. It is the part of Hegra most comparable to Petra in Jordan.

attribution: Radosław Botev — CC BY 3.0 pl, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Old mud-brick houses of the abandoned old town of AlUla beneath the cliffs
caption: The old town of AlUla, a maze of mud-brick houses that were inhabited until the 1980s. It is the town stop of the concept, and the place to see the Islamic-period settlement beside the Nabataean and Lihyanite sites.

photographer: Expedition 16 Crew Member on the International Space Station, NASA
attribution: Expedition 16 Crew Member on the International Space Station, NASA — Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Satellite view of the Harrat Khaybar volcanic field, a dark lava plateau with small craters, taken from the International Space Station
caption: The Harrat Khaybar lava field seen from the ISS (an astronaut photograph, not a ground view). It shows the scale of the black basalt plateau the concept would cross between AlUla and Hail.

commonsFile: File:View of Aarif Fort, Hail, Saudi.jpg
attribution: Iain Cheyne — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A'arif Fort, a historic fortress in the city of Hail
caption: A'arif Fort in Hail, the regional centre for the Jubbah and Shuwaymis rock art. It shows the historic urban setting of the northern leg of the route.
